> Why isn't `src/lib/index.ts` in `src/widgets/index/`?

The widgets are the binding between the connector + the Vanilla renderer. It's not the case for this one which is renderer agnostic. That's why it's inside `lib` rather than `widgets`, it is part of the "core" of InstantSearch.

body: Why not check for `helper` instead of `localInstantSearchInstance` (they are both initialized at the same place and I would avoid the `!` next line).

Both are equivalent if we remove the check against `localInstantSearchInstance` for `helper`, we remove the `!` for one but we'll have to add it on the other. I used this approach at first for almost all the places where we use `!` inside the module. I wrapped all usages inside a condition but it's "incorrect". The values **are** defined at that point, it adds complexity that is **not** necessary. We only add those conditions to make the compiler happy, it doesn't change the behavior of the code. 

Then the problem is how the code is structured. I agree with this. The current architecture does not scale very well with the approach I took for multiple indices, but it works for now and it's "simple" enough. If we revamp the core at some point we have to take those constraints into consideration.

It think that the reasoning behind @samouss' decision is that when we'll create several InstantSearch packages (e.g. `instantsearch-core`, `instantsearch-vanilla`, etc.), `index` will be exported from `instantsearch-core` because it doesn't include anything related to rendering. Thus it makes sense not to consider it as a widget but still to export it in `instantsearch-vanilla`, which right now is the `widgets/` folder.

Is that right @samouss?
